gaps.fact: Sicilia DOC (the Court's Sicily DOC), the island wide denomination of 2011 that replaced the regional IGT and has held varietal Grillo and Nero d'Avola to itself since 2017. Only the sicily article teaches it; no chapter fact and no stem names it.

Cannonau di Sardegna DOC, the island wide denomination for Cannonau. The chapters teach the grape and not the denomination, and the name stands only as a distractor in c-z6e95p7o; the article holds its rules.

The producers a candidate would recommend at service (Planeta, Donnafugata, Tasca d'Almerita, Benanti, Florio on Sicily; Argiolas, Sella & Mosca, Cantina Santadi on Sardinia). Both articles teach them; no stem of either bank asks an island producer.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (Italy), Village 61 (Italy Central & South), 122 in all; both categories are shared with the other Italian subjects, and by stem the islands' share is 7 Régionale (i-r8bf7n3v, i-lvhba6ar, i-ua2bzjrx, i-korw3y3l, i-5qvxafzi, i-ibc8sory, i-fggnpcko) and 13 Village (Sicily 7: c-2yz4dfi7, c-ovzebh73, c-p0sfeptr, c-g07ci2de, c-lf68sc81, c-kc34mg58, c-igxh381h; Sardinia 6: c-z6e95p7o, c-rfcq4y3d, c-ge32aayd, c-9u9vg1ia, c-18etdwil, c-kb9j840l). Beyond the map: Fortified Wines holds four Marsala stems, Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet three (i-vgcsf003, i-9e023msc, i-ufla9mjn), Dessert & Sweet Wines i-nny2fmxc (Zibibbo), Grapes & Labels i-7rkuqdmt (Nero d'Avola) and i-vjbga8vs (Vermentino's names), Jura, Savoie & Corsica c-8w73dbd5 (Vermentinu). The island page is well served: every grape the Court names, Etna's two colours and its contrade, Cerasuolo di Vittoria and Marsala's grades and sweetness words all have stems; the two island wide DOCs and the producers are the gaps. No factual error found: Cerasuolo di Vittoria DOCG 2005 (Nero d'Avola 50 to 70, Frappato 30 to 50), Etna DOC 1968 with Rosso at 80 per cent Nerello Mascalese and Bianco Superiore from Milo at 80 per cent Carricante, Marsala 1773 and its grades (Fine 1, Superiore 2, Superiore Riserva 4, Vergine 5, Stravecchio 10), Grillo as Catarratto crossed with Zibibbo, Vermentino di Gallura DOCG 1996, Cannonau di Sardegna 1972 and Carignano del Sulcis 1977 all hold. One Court cell to read with care: it prints Sicily: Islands off the southern tip of Italy, plural, for the one island. Two searches spent, both on Etna. The consortium voted on 10 November 2023 to seek DOCG and no decree had been published by September 2026 (vinous.com, September 2026; rivistadiagraria.org, October 2025), so Etna remains a DOC and Cerasuolo di Vittoria the island's only DOCG, as every Codex line says. A report that commune names may appear on Etna labels from the 2026 vintage (vinous.com) could not be confirmed against a decree, so it is not logged as a court update; the article already teaches the contrade.
